simple.meaning: גָּמַר (gâmar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to end (in the sense of completion or failure).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Psalms, beginning at Psalms 7:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּמַר (H1584) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּמַר (gâmar) / H1584 is traced through Psalms 7:10, Psalms 12:2, Psalms 57:3, Psalms 77:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1584. gamar גָּמַר verb end, come to an end, complete (only Psalms) (Late Hebrew id. complete ; Assyrian gamâru Lotz TP.Register & derivatives COT Gloss and others; Aramaic גְּמַר , ; Ethiopic (II); compare also Arabic collect, assemble ) — Qal Perfect ׳גּ Psa 12:2 ; 77:9 ; Imperfect יִגְמֹר 138:8 ; יִגְמָרֿ 7:10 ; Participle גֹּמֵר 57:3 ; — 1 come to an end, be no more Psa 7:10 ; 12:2 (|| [ מָּסַס ]); 77:9 (|| אָפֵס ). 2 transitive bring to an end, complete , עָלָ֑י גֹּמֵר אֵל Psa 57:3 God that completeth, accomplisheth, for me ( ᵐ5 Gr Bi גמל , & so Che doubtfully), ׳י בַּעֲדִי יִגְמֹר 138:8 .
